title: Glessner House's tall stone courses stand deeper
items: The tall granite courses on the Glessner house now throw a deeper shadow under their lower edges than the short ones, as a photograph from about 1888 shows. Through that photograph's own camera the tall-to-short ratio was 0.86 and is now 1.33, against the photograph's 1.32.

The stable's stone cupola is now laid in rough-faced courses, where it had smooth plates. Its shaft has four courses and each row of pigeon holes is one course between its ledges, as an 1887 print shows it.
